John found himself intrigued, wandering alone through the halls he could not help but feel a childish sense of curiosity nibbling bite by bite at his focus. So much equipment scattered the rooms and desks that had all been but abandoned. There was an eerie, lonely yet exciting aura within each room. “342A, B, C, 343 … 343H!” John counted in his thoughts,  scanning overhead the lab openings as he paced deeper into the facility, deeper into the mountain. Lab 343H had it’s blast doors sealed. “What secrets are you hiding that the Commander wants kept” John thought to himself. he stood firmly against the door. He locked his mag boots to the steel grate below him. The terminal on the door had been fried, destroyed. “went to a bit of effort on this one. Hmph”

John began cutting a hole at the centre of the door his suit’s  built in cutting torch extruded from the suit's wrist brace. Intended for ship repairs the tooling of the suit was useful in many scenario’s even breaching. A minute passed, John had cut out a hole large enough for his suits gauntlets to fit in and pry the doors open. He first inserted an Echo drone to check the close was clear. The scan revealed nothing but the usual scattered relics of the past computer systems, server stacks, although this room felt different. The equipment was larger, with a network of thick cabling was strewn across the lab floors like a tree's root system had been left to run wild.

John let out a prolonged strained grunt as the combined strength of him and his suit pried the door open. He stepped through and immediately the

gliding his finger tips over the countless unfamiliar relics from what seemed like a different age, but current to the day in their robustness. Instruments of science and engineering, Scattered in random, hinting at the life which once walked the halls. John found himself pulled into the remains of the abandoned facility eager to locate something missing. something seemed to be calling to him. This unexpected curiosity went against all his training, off guard. Johns trained state of caution and professionalism had been calmed by beauty. Elegantly designed human like machine arms clad plated with soft yet hardened alloys, humanly skin like feel to touch and look, met with course and exposed bearing linkages shoulder mounts grounded the witness to the mechanical nature. Amidst the scattered remnants of the room A dimly lit terminal posed itself to johns eye. It’s green light dancing off the alloys scattered through the room.  Several options poised Johns curiosity across the terminal. John knew the potential consequences, insubordination, court marshal, dishonourable discharge. All the outcomes rushed through his mind fighting against the undying curiosity that something just did not seem right. For decades fear was bestowed upon them through what now seemed like propaganda. It was told that the facility had been overthrown in a hostile takeover, yet no signs of resistance or violence were present. The facility was abandoned and it seemed to have also been the nature of what had occurred. No weapons fire, disposed munitions, no bodies. Just remnants of marvels of design left to wither incomplete. If this was the case why were kill orders placed on confirmed sightings. What was the need to attain the data drives if their was no sign or evidence of resistance. Would the alliance not have copies already secured of everything they  needed? What minimal information led him and his men to believe a salvage operation.

PRESS RESPECTIVE KEY FOR FOLLOWING:

	1.	HMNI Test Results.

	2.	Initiate HMNI Mobility Interface.

	3.	Initiate HMNI Neural Interface.

	4.	Initiate Full HMNI Interface.

	5.	New Entry.

	HMNI Test Results.

	1.	HMNITN1.

	2.	HMNIWT1.

	3.	HMNIWT2.

Project Fore Word, Doctor G.Wolfgang

The ability to interface with the ether of not only electric energy spectrum seamlessly, A spectrum that lives in the body riding the flow through the blood like an invisible seamless network shaped like mycelium formed by strong currents. Becoming hyper focused the patient could tap in and accelerate their blood, generating energy to the frontal lobe simultaneously powering the communications module.   “1” again.

	HMNITN1 Human Machine Neural Interface Test Notes 1:

After becoming integrated following the HMNI Neural Integration with the facility I feel as though my nerves extend miles of cold yet spiking wire and steel, every actuation I feel like a tingling sensation in my body, an extension of my own synapses. Every flickering light, closing door, rewritten data block. I am plugged in, one with the facility. Systems running at 98% due to the set-backs ordered by the overhaul to rewrite interfaces for weapon trajectory control by commander illus. Interface control synapse reaction time has been measured highly responsive at 1 micro-Second, not considering the hardware response delays. Test commands are currently limited and continued to test operations. The interface upon closing my eyes feels like flying across a grid. Controlled by my mental visions’ direction. I can target highlighted nodes which represent and actuators, thanks to the ideation of our brilliant minds here at the facility. The control interface feels almost seamless and intuitive. All in all the test has been a complete but concerning test. Commander Illus seems to be ever determined to twist the program to his own “Scientific Will” as he explains it.

“There are larger threats at play here that we all can’t consider without the United World Facilities, you would be swift to understand this Doctor! There are those in the system that won’t understand the project”

My interpretation of the Commander is that he will stop at nothing to deliver utmost solar and galactic rule through the system by harnessing the sentient technology.

…This concludes Test1.

Hitting Escape. John struggled to grasp what he was reading. He knew little of computer science, his training focused predominantly on survival, combat and rules of engagement to promote minimal loss of life, on both sides. However, this scientist wrote in simple terms giving clarity to what seemed a harmless interface between human and machine.

John lingered around the room captivated and overwhelmed by an age before his time. Stainless steel mechanical keyboards rusting silently away in the shadows, towered over by large vertical monitors over a century old. The old laboratory invoked Nostalgia of his grandfather’s lab tucked away on their farm lab before artificial vertical farming took over. Yet seamlessly preserved. A flickering light whispered across the room as robotic arms loomed seeming to track John’s movement across the shadows. John could feel the lab watching him, luring him towards a dimly lit corner of the lab, an ethereal luminescence pulsates, the chirping static of a struggling light bulb, pulling John in step by step, a colossal steel capsule nestled by the shadows, it’s secrets veiled in the flickering dance of light and darkness.

The capsule extruded from the ground all the way to an elevated ceiling which cratered upwards into an amalgamation of pipes and wires feeding from the walls into the foreboding mass of the capsule. The base however presented a humble opening, only human size yet not to the scale of it’s towering height and girth. As John approached closer the seams around the tiny door let out a sharp hiss, spewing steam and dust into the air in a sequence from top to bottom. The door retracted inwards then grinded softly, slowly to the side, inviting the John into its embrace. John found himself lured to this device. As he ran his hand across the door, A military stencil ran in his hands wake, “Cross Integration Chamber”. The room seemed to hum, whispering to him. John felt something deep seated inside him take hold of him, like he could no longer control his own body. He could not veer into the chamber and it’s internal workings, what secrets behold beyond it’s door. He checked his teams vitals one last time before actuating the helmet release from his suit. A sharp click and he had disconnected his helmet from the Mark IV.

The back of the suit splayed outwards, it’s rear armour like steel feathers formed the figure of wings, dimly lit now dancing before the chamber with the flickering ambience. John’s body suit shimmered his muscles flexed as he pulled himself from the suit, to a crisp kiss as his feet touched the cold steel grates of the laboratory leaving a pool of gelatinous goop from the neural sync pool within his suit. Like a possessed child being called back to the womb, John slowly undressed. The cold of the room sent chills, his hairs standing on end, unfaltering to the cold he stepped along the grate closer to the Pod’s embrace then paused at it’s opening gently laying his hand on it’s shell. He took one deep breath, and it was done.

John stepped inside the chamber. Suddenly the chamber door closed, sealing him in a pool of pitch-black darkness. A hiss splurted out, as a sleeping agent filled the pod enveloping John’s tattered body with dreams of never-ending tunnels reaching out and onwards like mycelium through a vast network extending far beyond the reaches of the stars he knew. Needle like pinches could be felt all over his body, they weren’t painful, but a pleasant feeling after the first few. Then all fell silent, Johns head fell heavy on his shoulders into a deep sleep, he was at peace in a dream that extended time space and the body itself.
